headline: Biophysical plausibility as a design and evaluation criterion for neural models
label: Biologically Plausible Neural Models
summary: Three recent preprints assess biological plausibility of neural models across plasticity, biophysics, and representational geometry.
synthesis: The dominant thread is biological realism as an explicit constraint on neural models, though the three preprints differ in modality. BrainFuse couples Hodgkin-Huxley biophysical neuron simulation with gradient-based learning in one differentiable infrastructure, aiming to bridge biophysical fidelity and core AI methods. A separate analysis applies manifold analysis and a tubularity metric to a neural foundation model to assess whether its internal processing stages are biologically plausible. The voltage imaging study addresses the measurement side, simulating how scanning versus wide-field temporal sampling affects the fidelity of voltage spike detection. What is new is the attempt to evaluate plausibility at several levels: biophysical dynamics in simulation, representational geometry in trained models, and the observability of spikes in imaging data. None of the items reports clinical validation.
